environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed on ECS Fargate with PostgreSQL RDS. The container runs with a read-only filesystem and drops all capabilities except CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE. The ECS task uses awsvpc networking with a security group that allows egress ONLY to the RDS endpoint on port 5432 and to an internal ECR pull-through cache on port 443 — all other outbound traffic is denied by explicit deny-all outbound rules with only those two CIDR-scoped exceptions. The PostgreSQL connection uses a restricted role 'invoice_app' with RLS force-enabled (ALTER ROLE invoice_app SET row_security = on; ALTER TABLE invoices FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY). Additionally, the ECS task has a seccomp profile that blocks the connect() syscall to any address outside the VPC CIDR range (10.0.0.0/8), enforced via a custom seccomp JSON profile loaded at container runtime. The combination of network-layer egress restriction and seccomp-level connect() filtering means external entity resolution cannot reach any attacker-controlled server, and local file read is blocked by the read-only root filesystem with no sensitive files mounted.

config.sensitive_file_mounts: none (/etc/passwd is default container, no secrets mounted)
config.rls_policy: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on invoices table, role invoice_app cannot bypass
